newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.4 pct at 329.61.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.4 pct at 329.61.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.4 percent to 329.61 by the start on Tuesday.
Latin America rose 1.3 percent day-on-day to 637.86, Asia was down 0.5 percent at 264.96 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.9 percent at 156.33.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars, was up 0.54 percent day-on-day at 178.52 at 1215 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.29 percent at 530.448, calculated after the close of trade on Friday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.44 percent to 127.01 by the start of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.70 percent at 105.43, Asia rose 0.10 to 133.63 and East Europe was up 0.95 at 158.47.
